title: The Demethoxy Derivatives of Curcumin Exhibit Greater Differentiation Suppression in 3T3-L1 Adipocytes Than Curcumin: A Mechanistic Study of Adipogenesis and Molecular Docking.
authors: Alalaiwe, Ahmed; Fang, Jia-You; Lee, Hsien-Ju; Chiu, Chun-Hui; Hsu, Ching-Yun
one_liner_zh: 该文研究姜黄素衍生物对3T3-L1脂肪细胞分化的抑制机制，虽含分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题TF-DNA结合建模关联弱。
abstract: Curcumin is a known anti-adipogenic agent for alleviating obesity and related disorders. Comprehensive comparisons of the anti-adipogenic activity of curcumin with other curcuminoids is minimal. This study compared adipogenesis inhibition with curcumin, demethoxycurcumin (DMC), and bisdemethoxycurcumin (BDMC), and their underlying mechanisms. We differentiated 3T3-L1 cells in the presence of curcuminoids, to determine lipid accumulation and triglyceride (TG) production. The expression of adipogenic transcription factors and lipogenic proteins was analyzed by Western blot. A significant reduction in Oil red O (ORO) staining was observed in the cells treated with curcuminoids at 20 muM. Inhibition was increased in the order of curcumin < DMC < BDMC. A similar trend was observed in the detection of intracellular TG. Curcuminoids suppressed differentiation by downregulating the expression of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARgamma) and CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein alpha (C/EBPalpha), leading to the downregulation of the lipogenic enzymes acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC) and fatty acid synthase (FAS). AMP-activated protein kinase alpha (AMPKalpha) phosphorylation was also activated by BDMC. Curcuminoids reduced the release of proinflammatory cytokines and leptin in 3T3-L1 cells in a dose-dependent manner, with BDMC showing the greatest potency. BDMC at 20 muM significantly decreased leptin by 72% compared with differentiated controls. Molecular docking computation indicated that curcuminoids, despite having structural similarity, had different interaction positions to PPARgamma, C/EBPalpha, and ACC. The docking profiles suggested a possible interaction of curcuminoids with C/EBPalpha and ACC, to directly inhibit their expression.
abstract_zh: 姜黄素是一种已知的抗脂肪生成剂，用于缓解肥胖及相关疾病。关于姜黄素与其他姜黄素类化合物抗脂肪生成活性的全面比较研究较少。本研究比较了姜黄素、去甲氧基姜黄素（DMC）和双去甲氧基姜黄素（BDMC）对脂肪生成的抑制作用及其潜在机制。我们在姜黄素类化合物存在下分化3T3-L1细胞，以测定脂质积累和甘油三酯（TG）生成。通过Western blot分析脂肪生成转录因子和脂质生成蛋白的表达。在20 μM姜黄素类化合物处理的细胞中，观察到油红O（ORO）染色显著减少。抑制作用按姜黄素 < DMC < BDMC的顺序增强。在细胞内TG检测中观察到类似趋势。姜黄素类化合物通过下调过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体γ（PPARγ）和CCAAT/增强子结合蛋白α（C/EBPα）的表达来抑制分化，导致脂质生成酶乙酰辅酶A羧化酶（ACC）和脂肪酸合酶（FAS）的下调。BDMC还激活了AMP活化蛋白激酶α（AMPKα）的磷酸化。姜黄素类化合物以剂量依赖性方式减少3T3-L1细胞中促炎细胞因子和瘦素的释放，其中BDMC效力最强。与分化对照组相比，20 μM BDMC使瘦素显著降低72%。分子对接计算表明，姜黄素类化合物尽管结构相似，但与PPARγ、C/EBPα和ACC的相互作用位置不同。对接图谱提示姜黄素类化合物可能与C/EBPα和ACC直接相互作用，从而抑制其表达。
